To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a package of dietary, exercise, and behavioral advice to overweight and obesity pregnant women to limit weight gain was not effective in improving maternal and infant health outcomes.

a lifestyle intervention in pregnancy to limit gestation weight gain in overweight/obese women reduces large-for-gestational age (LGA) infants and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and improves maternal glycaemic control and insulin sensitivity in pregnancy, but does not reduce caesarean section, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy or neonatal hypoglycaemia.

the LIMIT trial was a large, multicentre, randomised controlled trial of 2,180 pregnant women that found the implementation of a dietary and lifestyle intervention package to limit weight gain in overweight or obese women did not improve health outcomes for the woman or her infant.

the prevention of obesity in women of childbearing age and in their offspring.
the development and evaluation of an intervention to limit gestational (pregnancy) weight gain in overweight or obese women during pregnancy.
the development of effective interventions to improve the health outcomes of overweight and obese women and their infants during pregnancy.

the trial is designed to test the hypothesis that dietary and lifestyle intervention in obese and overweight pregnant women to limit weight gain during pregnancy will result in a reduction in large for dates infants and a reduction in other adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant.
the LIMIT trial was a well conducted randomised controlled trial of the effect of dietary and lifestyle interventions to prevent excessive gestational weight gain on maternal and infant outcomes.

Limiting gestational weight gain in overweight or obese women during pregnancy is not effective in preventing the development of large for gestational weight infants, or reducing other maternal or infant adverse health outcomes, however, it may be beneficial in reducing gestational weight gain.

our research is aimed at improving the health of women and infants in pregnancy.
the study was conducted as planned, and the data analysis is currently in progress.

the best way to improve the health of women and their babies is by helping them achieve a healthy weight before they become pregnant.
women who are overweight or obese during pregnancy can safely and successfully limit weight gain during pregnancy and that this intervention improves health outcomes for the mother and baby.
the best way to prevent excessive weight gain in pregnant women is to provide them with a structured program of diet, physical activity and behavioral support.
